bisc.note: Mainland grounds close at 5:30 p.m. Seeing the night sky here means a boat and island camping.

chis.note: Reached only by boat from Ventura or Santa Barbara. Seeing the night sky means camping on an island.

dena.note: One road entrance. In summer, private cars may drive only to Savage River, Mile 15 of the park road.

drto.note: Boat or seaplane only. Seeing the night sky means camping on Garden Key, reached by ferry or private boat.

gaar.note: No roads enter the park. Fly in by air taxi, or hike in from the Dalton Highway, and camp in the backcountry.

glba.note: No road leads to Glacier Bay. Fly or ferry to Gustavus, then camp or stay at the lodge in Bartlett Cove.

hale.note: Driving into the summit between 3 and 7 a.m. needs a sunrise reservation. Overnight only in campgrounds.

isro.note: Ferry or seaplane only, mid-May to September. Closed Nov 1 to Apr 15. Night skies mean staying on the island.

katm.note: Reached by small plane or boat from King Salmon. Brooks Camp campground and lodge run June 1 to Sept 17.

kefj.note: Exit Glacier is reached by road from Seward. The fjords themselves are seen by boat or plane.

kova.note: No roads reach the park. Fly from Kotzebue or Bettles by air taxi; the night sky means backcountry camping.

lacl.note: Not on the road system; most visitors arrive by small plane. Overnight means a lodge or backcountry camping.

npsa.note: Reached by flights to Pago Pago on Tutuila; smaller flights continue to Ofu and Taʻū. Plan travel early.

noca.note: SR 20 crosses the park but usually closes past Ross Dam Trailhead, November to April. Stehekin has no road in.

viis.note: Reached by passenger ferry or car barge from St. Thomas. Camping is only at Cinnamon Bay, by reservation.

voya.note: Visitor centers are reachable by car. Nearly every campsite is reached by boat.

wrst.note: Two long gravel roads reach the park, McCarthy and Nabesna. There is no fuel along either.
